name: Double Under Side Swing
description: A side swing feeds directly into a double under — the swing's arm momentum is what powers the extra rotation, so the double under here comes from timing and swing speed rather than a bigger jump.
tips: Let the swing build speed for 2-3 reps before committing to the double — a slow swing can't power two passes.
The transition happens at your hip height; don't lift your hands to chest height to 'help' the rope around.

name: Double Dutch Entry
description: Two turners swing a pair of ropes in opposite, overlapping circles while a third person reads the gap and jumps in without a rope in hand — the hardest part is entirely about timing, not jump technique. A good family trick: two people turn while a third practices the entry.
tips: Watch the rope closest to you, not both ropes — it tells you exactly when the gap opens.
Step in on a small bounce rather than a big jump; you can always jump bigger once you're inside and settled.
